Allenby Bridge.fact: The next destruction occurred during the 1967 Six-Day War, after which was replaced in 1968 with a temporary truss-type bridge.

Allenby Bridge.subject: International Relations
Allenby Bridge.question: Being _____ (1,250 ft) below sea level, it is the lowest fixed water crossing in the world
Allenby Bridge.fact: Being 381 metres (1,250 ft) below sea level, it is the lowest fixed water crossing in the world.

Allenby Bridge.subject: International Relations
Allenby Bridge.question: The 1922 census lists 12 people (8 _____ and 4 Muslims) living at the bridge
Allenby Bridge.fact: The 1922 census lists 12 people (8 Christians and 4 Muslims) living at the bridge. The 1931 census lists 13 people (11 Muslims and 2 Christians) living at the bridge.

Allenby Bridge.subject: International Relations
Allenby Bridge.question: In 1994, subsequent to the _____-Jordan peace treaty, a new modern paved crossing was constructed adjacent to the older wooden one with the aid of the Japanese government
Allenby Bridge.fact: In 1994, subsequent to the Israel-Jordan peace treaty, a new modern paved crossing was constructed adjacent to the older wooden one with the aid of the Japanese government. The Jordanian authorities recognize the bridge as an international border entry point, but neither Jordan nor Israel grant entry visas to foreign passport holders at this crossing, unlike the country's other border crossings with territory under Israeli control, nor stamp the passports of departing travelers.
